html:
José Batlle y Ordóñez was the president of Uruguay from 1903 to 1907 and from 1911 to 1915. He made it the first welfare state in Latin America.

A newspaper editor and leader of the Colorado Party, he ended the last civil war against the rural Blanco party in 1904. Then he brought in reforms far ahead of their time: the eight-hour day in 1915, pensions, free secondary schooling, divorce at the wife's request, and the abolition of the death penalty. He separated Church and state and created state companies for electricity, banking and insurance.

He even proposed replacing the presidency with a council, which was tried for a time. His reforms, paid for by beef and wool exports, made Uruguay known as the Switzerland of America. They shaped the country through the 1900s, until the crisis and dictatorship of the 1970s, and still underlie its social policies, such as cannabis reform.
sum: José Batlle y Ordóñez was the president of Uruguay from 1903 to 1907 and from 1911 to 1915. He made it the first welfare state in Latin America.
